oneOf.description: Hello (must be first).
A request; `seq` is unique per connection and echoed in the response.
Subscribe to events; the server replies with a `Subscribed` response.

from_cursor.description: Resume point; absent means "from a fresh snapshot".

oneOf.description: Stop a subscription.

AccountName.description: Remote account name on a destination.

oneOf.description:
Launch a program without a shell under the binding (spec §10.4). The runtime
never launches; the CLI does. `argv` never crosses IPC (Q8, ADR-0007 §8):
the request names the resolved executable and the holder process.
Produce a bound consumer configuration for a consumer Heimdall cannot launch.

BindScope.description:
Where an endpoint binds (ADR-0012 §2.1). Anything but `loopback` or `none` needs a
recorded consent.

oneOf.description: No bind (relay-only).
Loopback only (the default).
One non-loopback interface address (a widening).
A wildcard bind (a widening).

CaFingerprint.description:
⟨M03⟩ A CA public key's fingerprint: `SHA256:` followed by exactly 43 characters
of unpadded standard base64 (`A-Za-z0-9+/`), as `ssh-keygen -l` prints it
(m03-plan §5 item 1). Validated on parse and on decode; compared exactly.

Capability.description: Credential capabilities a caller may request (spec §7.2).

oneOf.description: SSH user authentication.
Git commit/tag signing (never implied by authentication; spec §7.2).
Agent forwarding (explicit, disabled by default; spec §8.5).
Create or replace a destination.
Remove a destination.
Adopt an existing identity.
Remove an adopted identity.
Create or replace a profile.
Remove a profile.

Declare an identity's interaction; always creates a `DeclareInteraction`
decision (QR1), completed only by an attended `decide`.

Withdraw a declaration (narrowing; no decision). Answered with
[`WithdrawDeclarationData`].

revision.description:
Expected revision: with it the withdrawal is a compare-and-swap, and a
newer declaration stays live (`withdrawn: false`).

oneOf.description:
⟨M03⟩ The ninth action (m03-plan §5 item 4b): a pair's preferred mechanism.
Journaled under `catalog`, local only. `managed_certificate` is refused
(`pair_not_enrolled`) without a `verified` enrollment for the pair; the
preference takes effect for P only through `setup apply`.

⟨M05⟩ Revision 5 (m05-plan §4 item 4): apply a portable bundle's catalog intent in
one journaled reconciliation (owner only, no decision: it creates no authority;
ADR-0011 I4). Served from M05 U7 (ADR-0006 §17.9): it adds the destinations and
profiles the catalog lacks and reports every other entry, never overwriting one.

dry_run.description:
⟨M05⟩ Revision 5.1 (§17.9): validate the bundle as a real import does, compute
the plan and answer it marked as a dry run, **writing nothing** (no catalog row,
operation, idempotency, event or journal record: a read). Owner only and gated
on `trusted-work/1`, as a real import. Omitted when false.

request_id.description: Idempotency request ID (not consulted by a dry run).

oneOf.description:
⟨M05⟩ Revision 5.1 (ADR-0006 §17.9; orchestrator ruling I-6): set or clear an
environment's default-profile **preference** (ADR-0011 §5.1). Owner only, no
decision (a preference is never authority: only a new request that omits its
profile reads it, and a running binding never does), journaled under `catalog`.
Needs `trusted-work/1`.

environment.description: The environment the preference belongs to; absent: the runtime's own.

profile.description: The default profile; `null` clears the preference. Always written.

interaction.description:
Interaction mode of this session. `non_interactive` sessions can never
become attended: `Attend` is refused with `INTERACTION_REQUIRED`
(ADR-0006 §3.1). Defaults to non-interactive when omitted.

remote_client.description:
⟨M06⟩ Revision 6 (ADR-0012 §3.6, §9 item 1): the paired client a runner's bridge
declares for this session. Omitted when absent, so every earlier hello is
byte-identical. A runtime that does not offer `remote-control/1` refuses a hello
carrying it with `SCHEMA_UNSUPPORTED` (wave 0: every runtime). It is never read
from a request field.

required.description:
Capabilities the client requires; a missing one is rejected explicitly
(spec §11.2 "required capability must be rejected explicitly"). Must be a
subset of the negotiated set (`capabilities ∩ server offer`), ADR-0006 §2.3.

ClientId.description:
⟨M06⟩ Revision 6 (ADR-0012 §3.6, §3.7): a paired management client, minted by the
runner at invitation (`cl_<32 hex>`). It names the enrollment line
(`heimdall-mgmt:<cid>`) and the bridge's argv; it is never a credential and never a
request field that sets a caller (ADR-0006 §18).

ConfirmTimeRequest.description:
Attended owner confirmation of the current wall time to resolve
`TIME_UNCERTAIN` after a reboot or sync loss (ADR-0005 §3.6). Never moves a
deadline; never rebuilds a budget. Attended sessions only.

observed_wall.description:
The wall time the owner confirms as correct now (RFC 3339 with offset). It
must agree with the runtime's own wall clock within tolerance; the owner
cannot set time, only vouch for it.

ConflictKind.description: A conflict a repair addresses (ADR-0007 §5.5, §5.7). Also a stable error reason.

oneOf.description: The user file changed since the plan.
The managed file was edited.
A marker line was edited.
A marker appears more than once.
The include block is conditional.
A target file cannot be managed (manual mode).
A managed alias collides with a user alias.
Another writer changed a file during the transaction.
Git's configuration lock is held.
A setup operation is held for the owner (ADR-0007 §5.7 outcome H).

⟨ADR-0007 §12.20 item 2⟩ A check the transaction requires could not run: B_git's
Git parse check (§5.6 step 3) with local queries disabled or no verified Git
client (§12.19 item 8). The item aborts before its commit point.

ConnectionId.description:
⟨M03⟩ Owned connection ID (an `owned_connections` row; ADR-0008 D8; m03-plan
§5 items 4, 4a). Runtime-generated; never a PID.

ConnectionRequest.description:
`EnsureRequest.connection` (§5 item 5): a request may only **narrow** `existing`
to `strict`; `graceful` in a request is `USAGE_ERROR` (checked by the
application). It enters the canonical hash only when present.

ConnectionsRequest.description:
`Request::Connections` (capability `connections/1`). Both actions are
synchronous, effectful, and accepted from the owner role only.

oneOf.description:
Close one owned connection (narrowing; no decision). kind
`"connections.close"`.

The Windows launcher's durable registration of the contained, still
suspended `ssh.exe` (ADR-0008 D8 item 2). kind `"connections.register"`.

image.description:
The child's image path (ADR-0008 D8 item 2, revision 3); the runtime
checks it is the verified client.

ControllerRecordRequest.description:
`Request::ControllerRecord`, tagged by `action` (ADR-0006 §18.7 item 6): write the
controller's own records of its runners through its runtime. Local owner only; a paired
session is refused. No form widens anything on a runner: the runner-side effects
(enrollment, revocation) are the management session's, confirmed where ADR-0012 §3.10
says.

oneOf.description:
Insert or replace the record of `record.environment`. Kind
`controller_record.put_environment`.

Forget one runner's record (absent: nothing to remove). Kind
`controller_record.remove_environment`.

⟨rev6.4; ADR-0006 §18.8 item 4; ADR-0012 §7.4 ⟨2026-11-21⟩⟩ Record the owner's
acknowledgement that the pauses and cutoffs named in `effects`, which this controller
delivered to the runner `environment`, were lifted there (`heimdall environment
resume-issuance`). It names the specific delivered effects the owner was shown and
releases only those: a pause or cutoff delivered later is not acknowledged by it.
Attended: a local owner in an attended session, after the CLI's typed confirmation.
An empty list, or an ID that is not a pause or cutoff this controller delivered to
`environment`, is refused whole with effect `none`. Issuance for that runner resumes
only when its authority report shows each lift as well; the acknowledgement alone
reopens nothing. Kind `controller_record.resume_issuance`.

effects.description: The delivered effects the owner was shown and confirmed lifted (at least one).

Cursor.description: Opaque, reader-scoped resumption token. Never parse it outside the runtime.

DeadlineIntent.description:
Deadline intent as given by the caller, kept verbatim so that a retry of
`--for 2h` hashes equal (spec §6.2, primitives-draft §5).

oneOf.description: RFC 3339 timestamp with explicit offset (machine requests must be unambiguous).
ISO 8601 / friendly duration string (`PT2H`, `2h`), converted once at creation.

DecideRequest.description:
Complete a pending decision (approval of added authority, a widening policy
action, or a time confirmation). Only accepted on an **attended** control
session; refused with `INTERACTION_REQUIRED` otherwise, and with
`DECISION_STALE` when the record was consumed, expired, or issued under an older
authority generation (ADR-0006 §3.1). Consume-once.

DecisionId.description: Server-issued decision record ID (ADR-0006 §3.1 attended confirmation).

DeclaredInteraction.description: The interaction an owner may declare (QR1). Only `none` exists.

oneOf.description: The key asks for no confirmation.

scope.description: Scope subset (must be within the parent).

until.description: Deadline intent (effective deadline must not exceed the parent's).

DestinationDefinitionSpec.description: How a managed destination is defined; an observed one stays in the user's file.

oneOf.description: Rendered into the managed file P.

identity.description: The adopted identity the alias uses.

jump.description:
⟨M04⟩ Revision 5 (ADR-0010 §5 item 1): the single-hop jump destination, a
catalog destination with one approved host key and no route of its own
(`route_chain_unsupported`). Omitted when absent; joint wave 0 refuses a
request that names one (`driver_unavailable`).

oneOf.description: Defined by the user; Heimdall only observes it.

DestinationScopeEnforcement.description: Destination-scope enforcement levels (spec §4.3), ordered weakest to strongest.

oneOf.description: Not known.
Intent only; nothing enforces it.
Client configuration routes to the destination.
Agent restriction authenticated to the destination (spec S03).
Server-side principal mapping verified by test.
A separately tested isolated execution boundary.

DestinationSpec.description: A destination as the caller specifies it.

oneOf.description:
Retire this controller device: revoke its client on every runner where it is
enrolled, then destroy K_mgmt. Needs an attended local decision (ADR-0012 §3.10
item 4). Kind `device.retire`.

DistributionGuid.description:
A WSL distribution's registration GUID under `HKCU\...\Lxss` (ADR-0010 §3 item 1): the
identity of a distribution, kept across renames; a re-registered distribution is a new
GUID. Wire form: 36 lowercase hex-and-hyphen characters, `8-4-4-4-12`, no braces
(validated on decode; the CLI normalizes case and strips braces before sending).

EffectId.description:
⟨M06⟩ Revision 6 (ADR-0012 §7.2): a narrowing effect, minted by its producing
controller. Keyed with the authenticated producer, the typed target and its
generation.

EffectTarget.description:
A typed narrowing effect's target (ADR-0012 §7.2). With the authenticated producing
controller (the session's client, never a field) and the effect ID, it keys the
effect; each target carries its own generation.

oneOf.description:
Applied as a durable grant tombstone (ADR-0005 §6.1 "Revocation"), acknowledged
with its enforcement state.

Applied as a durable policy revision: running grants continue, new activations
are refused (§6.1 "Pause"). Not a tombstone.

Applied as a durable policy revision that also ends every affected grant like
expiry and refuses new grants until cleared (ADR-0005 §6.1 "Cutoff").
⟨rev6.1; M06-W0-R02, orchestrator ruling⟩ It carries the owner's instant `at` (as the
local `policy cutoff` request does). The runner's effective cutoff is
`min(existing, at)`: a delivered or replayed cutoff only shortens it, never delays it
(moving a cutoff later is a widening, runner-local). An `at` at or before trusted now
applies at the durable apply, with no signature after that commit; a future `at` is
persisted and enforced at `at` by the supervisor wake; under uncertain time it fires
as soon as `at` may have passed (the upper bound of now). Enforcement is m06-plan U4's.

EndpointKind.description: The transport of an agent endpoint.

oneOf.description: A Unix-domain socket path.
A Windows named pipe name.

EndpointRef.description:
A reference to an agent endpoint. The locator is a path or pipe name, never a
secret; it is compared exactly (a changed locator lapses a declaration,
ADR-0007 §7).

oneOf.description: A `cert-authority` line in the account's registry (the default).
`TrustedUserCAKeys` plus `AuthorizedPrincipalsFile`, applied by the owner.

EnrollmentId.description:
⟨M03⟩ Enrollment record ID (m03-plan §5 item 1; ADR-0008 D5 §6.2). The remote
marker is `heimdall:<enrollment-id>`, so the ID is the add's idempotency key.

oneOf.description:
Read-only, local, contacts nothing. kind `enrollment.preview`; data
[`EnrollmentPlan`].

Journaled `enrollment.apply`, effect class `remote_mutation`; needs
`EnrollAccount` (or `EnrollSystemForm`).
Journaled `enrollment.verify`, effect class `local`; never removes anything.

Journaled `enrollment.remove`, effect class `remote_mutation`; needs
`RemoveEnrollment` (system form: a typed confirmation).

Synchronous: drives an unresolved `enrollment.apply`/`remove` (ADR-0008 D5
§6.7). Owner role only; a redispatch of an append needs an attended session.

after_manual_recovery.description: After the owner removed a lock by hand: classify only, never redispatch.

oneOf.description:
Synchronous, owner channel: record abandonment (residual
`pending_until_line_removed`).

Synchronous, owner role only: the next client-executed step (ADR-0008 D5
§6.3). kind `enrollment.step`.

Synchronous, owner role only: the CLI's result for the outstanding step.
kind `enrollment.step_result`.

stderr_excerpt.description: At most 4 KiB, redacted, diagnostics only.

stdout.description: At most 512 KiB of HM1 lines.

account.description:
Default: the managed definition's account; any other value is `USAGE_ERROR`
(`account_override_refused`).

ca_fingerprint.description: CA; default the newest active CA.

connection.description:
⟨M03⟩ Narrow the existing-connections mode to `strict` (§5 item 5). Enters
the canonical hash only when present, so M01/M02 hashes are unchanged.

context.description:
⟨M05⟩ Revision 5 (m05-plan §4 item 1): the caller's working directory; the
runtime resolves the workspace from it (ADR-0011 §2.2, §3.2). Absent: personal
context, exactly the M01–M03 request. Omitted when absent; the canonical hash's
context extras exist only when it is present (revision 5 §17 item 4).

covered_only.description:
⟨M05⟩ Revision 5: activate only the subset the context's policy already covers,
never create a decision, and report the rest as `uncovered` (background
triggers; ADR-0011 §3.2). Omitted when false.

pair_issuers.description:
⟨rev6.4; ADR-0006 §18.8 item 1; ADR-0012 §4 item 2 ⟨2026-11-21⟩⟩ Per
destination/account pair, the fingerprint of the CA the controller will issue from.
Set by the forwarding controller, or by the runner's local owner for a CA already in
the runner's `issuer_trust` (that admits a pending grant only). A runner resolves a
named pair to `managed_certificate` only when that CA is in its `issuer_trust` for
the party that named it, and refuses `issuer_untrusted` otherwise; nothing about
such a pair comes from the runner's own catalog. Omitted when empty, so every
earlier request and its canonical hash are unchanged.

profile.description:
Profile, or a subset of it via `scope`. ⟨M05⟩ Revision 5: optional only when
`context` is present (the workspace's manifest or trust record, else the personal
default profile, names it); a request with neither is `USAGE_ERROR`. Every
M01–M03 request carries it, so its wire form and hash are unchanged.

profile_revision.description: Explicit profile revision; default latest at creation (pinned afterwards).

scope.description: Optional subset of the profile's destination/account pairs.

until.description: Deadline intent; default the policy's saved window.

EnvironmentRequest.description:
`Request::Environment`, tagged by `action` (m04-plan §5 item 2). Synchronous, owner
role, capability `environments/1`. Mode B and containers add a place where authority
can be realized, so each creates a decision record (ADR-0006 §3.1) and never executes
on dispatch; Mode A alone goes through the setup confirmation only.

oneOf.description:
Enable WSL integration for one distribution (ADR-0010 §2, §3). Kind
`environment.wsl_enable`.

account.description:
The Linux account chosen at enable (Mode B's environment identity, with the
GUID).

mode_a.description: Mode A: the distribution's Git uses the Windows in-box `ssh.exe`.

mode_b.description: Mode B: a Linux-native scoped endpoint through the supervised helper.

oneOf.description:
Disable it: release the environment's bindings, withdraw the endpoints, roll back
the distribution's projection, end the helper (ADR-0010 §3 item 13). Kind
`environment.wsl_disable`.

start.description:
The explicit authorized start of a stopped distribution so its cleanup runs
now (ADR-0010 §9 item 2); without it a stopped distribution's cleanup stays a
retained, reported obligation.

oneOf.description:
Create a container environment and its stable directory (ADR-0010 §4 item 1). Kind
`environment.container_add`.

label.description: The owner's label (1 to 64 bytes, no control characters).

oneOf.description:
Release the container environment's binding and remove its directory (ADR-0010 §4
item 6). Kind `environment.container_remove`.

EventType.description: Event types emitted by the runtime (spec §13.6 audit coverage).

oneOf.description: An operation changed state.
A grant changed state.
A standing policy changed (revision, pause, cutoff).
A managed resource changed desired/observed state or generation.
A credential lifecycle event (issued, renewed, expired, revoked).
An owner decision was requested or recorded.

The subscriber fell behind a bounded buffer; take a snapshot and resume
(spec §11.5 backpressure).
The runtime started or stopped (restart recovery boundary).

⟨M03⟩ An enrollment record changed state (payload
[`crate::managed::EnrollmentEventPayload`]).

⟨M03⟩ An owned connection started or closed (payload
[`crate::managed::ConnectionEventPayload`]).

⟨M03⟩ A session lock was observed (payload
[`crate::managed::SessionLockEventPayload`]).

⟨M05⟩ Revision 5 (m05-plan §4 item 8): a background activation was activated,
blocked or not covered (payload [`crate::trust::ActivationEventPayload`]). Not
emitted by joint wave 0.

⟨M06⟩ Revision 6 (ADR-0012 §9 item 8): `environment.connectivity_changed` (payload
[`crate::remote::EnvironmentEventPayload`]). Declared, not emitted by wave 0.

⟨M06⟩ Revision 6: `client.enrolled`, `client.revoked` (payload
[`crate::remote::ClientEventPayload`]). Declared, not emitted by wave 0.

⟨M06⟩ Revision 6: `device.retired` (payload [`crate::remote::DeviceEventPayload`]).
Declared, not emitted by wave 0.

⟨M06⟩ Revision 6: `remote_effect.pending`, `remote_effect.acknowledged` (payload
[`crate::remote::RemoteEffectEventPayload`]). Declared, not emitted by wave 0.

⟨M06⟩ Revision 6: `route.health` for every attempt, `route.failed_over` its subtype
(payload [`crate::route::RouteHealthPayload`]). Declared, not emitted by wave 0.

ExistingConnectionsMode.description:
What happens to owned dedicated connections at the admission deadline (ADR-0008
D8 item 1). `strict` is narrowing; `graceful` (the default) is widening.

oneOf.description: Existing dedicated sessions may stay connected (spec §6.6 default).
Owned connections are closed at the deadline.

ExposurePolicy.description:
One endpoint's effective exposure policy (ADR-0012 §2.1): the bind, relay map, peer
relay hints, direct addresses, lookup and ancillary targets are built from it alone,
and anything outside it is refused. The default is the minimal policy.

direct_fallback.description: Direct fallback to learned or public addresses (reveals public IPs; a widening).

port.description:
⟨rev6.3⟩ The serve port (ADR-0012 §2.1 ⟨2026-11-21⟩; `heimdall transport enable
--port <n>`). Omitted when none: the first successful bind's port is then recorded
durably and reused at every later start. `0` is refused. A port that cannot be bound
fails closed (`transport_unavailable`); changing it is `disable` then `enable`.

ForeignRemovalTarget.description:
The full public removal descriptor of an enrollment from a recovery bundle
(ADR-0008 D4 item 5; §17.1 item 11). The decision and the request hash cover
every field.

bundle_destination_id.description: The bundle's destination ID: a label only (IDs are per installation).

bundle_hostname.description:
Required (a redacted bundle is refused, `bundle_redacted`); must equal the
alias's evaluated `HostName` byte for byte (`bundle_host_mismatch`).

line_sha256.description: The full line's SHA-256 (hex); rebuilt and checked before connecting.

local_alias.description: This device's managed alias for the host.

IdentityId.description:
Adopted existing-access identity in the catalog (ADR-0007 §7; m02-plan §5
item 1). Runtime-generated at adoption; never derived from key material.

IdentitySourceSpec.description: Where an adopted identity is used from.

oneOf.description: A key held by a native agent at this endpoint.
A key held by the 1Password agent.

endpoint.description: The endpoint, when not the documented default.

oneOf.description: A public key file (the private key is never opened).

IdentitySpec.description:
An identity to adopt. Its interaction profile comes from ADR-0007 §7, not from
the request.

InfrastructureProfile.description:
Relay and lookup infrastructure (ADR-0012 §2.2). A route never falls back to a profile
it does not name.

oneOf.description: Direct only (the default).
The user's relay URLs, each consented.
n0's relays plus lookup: off by default and outside V1 unless its capture row runs.

InspectRequest.description:
`inspect` request (read-only; never contacts agents, network, or executable
configuration; spec §10.2).

cwd.description:
⟨M05⟩ Revision 5: the working directory `workspace` resolves ([`WorkContext`]'s
bounds). Omitted when absent.

preview.description: Dry-run authority preview: resolved snapshot plus authority delta.

redact.description:
⟨M05⟩ Revision 5: `export` redacts host names, addresses and labels. Omitted when
false.

oneOf.description: Capability and schema discovery (R-AP-08).
Known environments.
Profiles.
Destinations.
Bindings.
Grants.
Operations.
Pending owner decisions.

Catalog identities with fresh eligibility and each live declaration's
reference (M02).
Projection resources, read-only (M02).
⟨M03⟩ Enrollment records (`EnrollmentsView`).
⟨M03⟩ The issuer status (`IssuerStatus`).
⟨M03⟩ Owned connections (`ConnectionsView`).

⟨M05⟩ Revision 5 (m05-plan §4 item 5): the workspace the request's `cwd`
resolves to and its trust state (`crate::trust::WorkspaceView`).
⟨M05⟩ Every standing policy with its applied history (`crate::trust::PoliciesView`).

⟨M05⟩ A portable bundle of catalog intent (`crate::project::PortableBundle`),
redacted when the request says `redact`.

InteractionMode.description: Whether Heimdall may open prompts (spec §11.3; R-AP-06).

oneOf.description: Heimdall may present decisions on the owner channel.
Heimdall opens no browser, dialog, or terminal prompt.

InvitationId.description:
⟨M06⟩ Revision 6 (ADR-0012 §3.9): an invitation, minted by the runner with its
pending record. Consumed once by `join`'s compare-and-set.

IrohEndpointId.description:
⟨M06⟩ Revision 6 (ADR-0012 §1, §5.1): an Iroh endpoint ID, the endpoint's public key
as 64 lowercase hex characters. Reachability identity only: it grants nothing (spec
§8.6) and is distinct from every SSH and management key (ADR-0012 §0).

oneOf.description: Read-only. kind `issuer.status`; data [`IssuerStatus`].

Effectful, synchronous; always creates a `RegisterIssuer` decision and never
executes on dispatch (ADR-0006 §2.3 N04 pattern). kind `issuer.register`.
Covers init, rotate-begin and restore.

backup_created_at.description: When the backup bytes were prepared.

backup_sha256.description:
Hex SHA-256 of the exact D5 backup bytes prepared in memory before this
request; the bytes are written only after approval (ADR-0008 D4 item 1).

ca_public_key.description: OpenSSH one-line Ed25519 public key, no comment.

expected_store_locator.description:
⟨ADR-0008 §17.22 item 12⟩ A restore that wrote a new store item for a CA
whose record survives (D4 item 4, log intact; a re-registration of the
known CA): the locator it expects recorded now, compared and swapped for
`store_locator` on approval (absent: none recorded). A mismatch refuses and
changes nothing. The displaced item is listed in `orphan_store_items`.

rotation_of.description: Rotate-begin: the CA this one rotates.

store.description: The store the key will live in.

store_locator.description:
⟨ADR-0008 §17.22 item 12⟩ The ceremony's report of the K_ca store item it
wrote: the exact `StoreItemRef` locator its `put` returned (D4 item 1 step
6), bound to this CA, this installation and `store`. Sent again after the
put with the same registration: it joins the pending `RegisterIssuer`
decision, which records it, and the approval records it with the CA.
Absent before the put (step 3).

oneOf.description: Attended sessions only. kind `issuer.unlock`.

Creates a `RetireIssuer` decision. kind `issuer.retire`. On a CA whose
retirement waits at `unloaded`, answers the issuer status, which names the
store item to delete ([`CaStatus::store_locator`]).

deleted_locator.description:
⟨ADR-0008 §17.22 item 12⟩ The owner-present CLI's confirmation that it
deleted exactly this store item and a re-read found it absent (attended
sessions only): the CA's recorded locator while it is `unloaded` (the
record then reaches `retired`), or one of its displaced items listed in
`orphan_store_items` (it leaves the list). Anything else is refused and
changes nothing. The runtime never deletes a store item itself (D3).

oneOf.description:
Read-only; public metadata only. kind `issuer.bundle`; data
[`RecoveryBundle`].

redact_hostnames.description: Omit hostnames (foreign removal then refuses the bundle).

oneOf.description:
⟨ADR-0008 §17.25 item 8⟩ The CLI's confirmation that it wrote a recovery
bundle completely and fsynced it. kind `issuer.bundle_written`; synchronous
(it records `last_bundle_at` and the digest, which never lower). The record
never stores the file's path. Sent only after the write; a bundle the CLI
failed to write is never confirmed.

sha256.description:
Hex SHA-256 of the exact bytes written (lowercase, 64 characters; the
form of `Register.backup_sha256`).

KeyFingerprint.description:
⟨M06⟩ Revision 6 (ADR-0012 §3.9 item 1, §5.1, §9 items 5 and 9): an SSH public key's
fingerprint, `SHA256:` followed by exactly 43 characters of unpadded standard base64,
as `ssh-keygen -l` prints it (the same form as [`CaFingerprint`]). Used for pinned
host keys and for an invitation's receiving key. Validated on parse and on decode;
compared exactly.

executable.description:
The resolved executable: absolute, 1 to 4096 bytes, no NUL. A resolved path
that is not Unicode is refused locally (`LAUNCH_FAILED`, `refused_path`).

holder.description: The holder process (delivery metadata; not hashed).

LockBehavior.description:

PortableBundle.description:
A portable bundle (ADR-0011 I4; `inspect export`, `catalog apply_import`): catalog

redacted.description: Whether host names, addresses and labels were redacted.

reestablish.description:

host_key_fingerprints.description:

jump.description:

PortableIdentity.description: An identity reference in a bundle.

PreferredMechanism.description: The pair mechanism a `SetPreference` catalog action selects.

oneOf.description: Managed certificates (needs a verified enrollment: `pair_not_enrolled`).

agent_forward_refused.description: Agent forwarding, offered with a disposable agent, was refused.

ProcessHolder.description:
The process holding a binding reference: its PID and an opaque OS start-time

started_at.description: Opaque OS start-time token: 1 to 64 bytes of `[A-Za-z0-9._:-]`.

ProfileSpec.description: A profile as the caller specifies it.

ProjectionItem.description: A projection item: the OpenSSH projection or the Git include (ADR-0007 §5.4).

The Git include block B_git and the managed file P_git.

The canonical registry the bundle and foreign removal carry: the validated path

RemoteEnvironmentPin.description:
The controller's record of one paired runner environment: the authoritative document of

client.description: This device's client on that runner.

destination.description: The catalog destination that reaches it.

environment.description: The runner's environment ID, as its hello reported it.

RemoteEnvironmentRequest.description:
`Request::RemoteEnvironment`, tagged by `action` (ADR-0012 §3, §6.4, §9 item 6:

`request_id`, so a replay after the runner-local decision returns the recorded
terminal result (ADR-0012 §3.10 T-RA3).

oneOf.description:
Bootstrap a runner over the owner's existing, independently host-verified SSH
access to the runner account (ADR-0012 §3.3): install or verify the binary, run
`heimdall remote init`, enroll this controller's K_mgmt as `owner` (confirmed in
the bootstrap's interactive ssh session with a TTY). Also the repair path for a
lost host pin or K_mgmt. Kind `remote_environment.add`.

destination.description:
The catalog destination whose pinned host key and existing access reach the
runner account (never `ssh-keyscan`).

oneOf.description:
Create an invitation on the runner (ADR-0012 §3.9): a widening action, confirmed
runner-locally. The runner mints the invitation and client IDs. Kind

iroh_admission.description:
⟨rev6.3⟩ Whether the invited client may reach this runner over Iroh (ADR-0012
§2.3 item 1). Part of the invitation's exact request, so the runner-local widening

key_fingerprint.description:
The receiving key's fingerprint, which the owner confirmed against the new

public_key.description:

the runner can write the management line. The runner refuses it unless its
fingerprint equals `key_fingerprint`.

role.description: The role the invited client will hold.

oneOf.description:
⟨rev6.1⟩ The activation probe (ADR-0012 §3.2): the enrolled key's first session

nonce.description: The pending record's activation nonce, echoed.

oneOf.description:
Consume an invitation: `pending → active` only if the invitation, the client (from

iroh_endpoint.description:
⟨rev6.3⟩ The joining client's own Iroh endpoint ID, sent over its K_mgmt session

⟨rev6.3; ADR-0006 §18.7 item 16⟩ What the joining device's four confirming probes

RequestId.description: Caller-chosen request ID; part of the idempotency key (spec §11.4).

Make a route the most preferred. A pure preference change needs the routes'

⟨rev6.1; M06-W0-R08⟩ Optional idempotency key (ADR-0006 §7): a preference among

The endpoint is an adopted stock Pigeons roost: external infrastructure with

`Request::RunnerLocal`, tagged by `action` (ADR-0006 §18.7 item 7; ADR-0012 §3.10, §4.2,
§4.4): the runner's own `issuer_trust` and time-source designation, decided at the

oneOf.description:

`runner_local.trust_issuer`.

The CA's OpenSSH public key line (public text; the runner computes the

Designate a paired owner client as this runner's trusted time source (widening;
ADR-0012 §4.4). Kind `runner_local.designate_time_source`.
Stop trusting a CA (narrowing). Kind `runner_local.distrust_issuer`.
Clear the time-source designation (narrowing). Kind `runner_local.clear_time_source`.

⟨M06-W2-R02⟩ `heimdall remote init` while this runner's runtime runs (widening):
enroll a controller's management key as an owner client, or repair the enrollment of
the same key (its management line is written again; ADR-0012 §3.3). With

client.description: The client ID the controller records for itself.

The controller's management key (`ssh-ed25519 <base64>`, public text), at most

RunnerRequest.description:
`Request::Runner`, tagged by `action` (ADR-0012 §4, §7, §9 item 6): the requests a
controller sends a runner over the management channel. Capability `runner/1`. None

oneOf.description:
Ask the runner to generate K_env for a grant it admitted and return K_env.pub
bound to the grant and its generation (ADR-0012 §4.2 step 2). Kind
`runner.prepare_remote_grant`.

Install the issuer's certificate for that key (§4.2 step 4): the runner checks its
key, issuer (`issuer_trust`), principals, generation, scope and `valid_before`.
Kind `runner.install_certificate`.

certificate.description:
The OpenSSH certificate, one line of public text (at most
[`MAX_CERTIFICATE_BYTES`]).

oneOf.description:
Ask the runner for a fresh time-challenge nonce (ADR-0012 §4.4). Kind
`runner.time_challenge`.

Answer it as the runner's designated time source: fresh, nonce-bound, counted only
within the RTT bound; it may move an anchor earlier only (§4.4). Kind
`runner.time_response`.

Deliver a typed narrowing effect (ADR-0012 §7.2): acknowledged only after the
durable record it names exists. Kind `runner.deliver_effect`.

effect.description: The effect ID the producing controller minted.

oneOf.description:
The runner's authority report: tombstones, policy revisions with their
generations, installed certificates (§7.4 step 3), read by the issuer's

ShutdownRequest.description:
Ask the runtime to stop (ADR-0006 §13.6 item 8; capability
[`crate::ipc::capability::SERVICE_CONTROL_V1`]).

Accepted only from the owner principal on the control endpoint (never from a
limited consumer), on any session (attended or not: stopping the service is an
availability action, not a widening of authority; a same-user process could end
the process anyway). Idempotent: a repeated request while the runtime is
draining answers `OK` again. The runtime answers `OK {"stopping": true, ...}`
first, then drains gracefully: it stops accepting, lets in-flight operations
reach a durable stage (bounded; anything still running resumes through restart
recovery), persists, removes its advertisement and endpoints, and exits 0.
Not an operation: no operation ID, no idempotency record.

StoreKind.description:
The platform store holding K_ca (ADR-0008 D1). **No test variant**: the
test-only store kind lives in `heimdall-testkit`, outside the public schema
(F23).

oneOf.description: The macOS login keychain.
The macOS data-protection keychain.
Windows DPAPI (current user).
The Linux Secret Service.

TransportRequest.description:
`Request::Transport`, tagged by `action` (ADR-0012 §2, §9 item 6: `transport
enable|disable` and `roost adopt`). Capability `transport-iroh/1`.

oneOf.description:
Generate K_iroh in a verified platform store and, with `serve`, start the
supervised serve child (ADR-0012 §2.3, §2.4). Exposure beyond the minimal policy is
a widening action. Kind `transport.enable`.

exposure.description: The endpoint's exposure policy; the minimal policy when absent.

serve.description: Also serve this host's sshd to enrolled clients.

oneOf.description:
Stop serve, destroy K_iroh and remove every route that names it, with their
projections and allowlist entries (ADR-0012 §2.5). Kind `transport.disable`.

Adopt an existing stock Pigeons roost as a destination's Iroh route (ADR-0012
§2.8): a widening action bound to the roost's endpoint ID and disclosed exposure.
Kind `transport.adopt_roost`.

exposure.description: The dialer's exposure policy for it; the minimal policy when absent.

oneOf.description:
⟨rev6.3; ADR-0006 §18.7 item 10⟩ Rotate this device's K_iroh through the runtime (a
rotation, not a widening; ADR-0012 §2.4 item 4). Local owner only: a paired session
is refused `INTERACTION_REQUIRED`, reason `local_owner_required`. Retry-safe: the
new key is stored as a new item and the old one is never overwritten; each recorded
runner is sent `remote_environment.rotate_endpoint`, and one that fails stays
recorded as pending; running the form again finishes the pending runners and mints
no further key; the old K_iroh is destroyed only after every recorded runner has
acknowledged or been forgotten. The result names the runners still pending. Kind
`transport.rotate`.

TrustProposal.description:
What the owner approves in a `TrustWorkspace` decision (ADR-0011 §2.1): the request
the workspace makes (its manifest ∩ the latest profile snapshot, or the trust record's
own scope when there is no manifest), fixed at decision creation (I5).

background_work.description: Lock behaviour requested by `preferences.background_work`, shown at review.

pairs.description: Pairs (a subset of the profile; empty means the whole profile).

UninstallFenceRequest.description:
⟨M03; ADR-0008 §17.27 item 2 (W5-S01)⟩ The uninstall fence (capability
[`crate::ipc::capability::SERVICE_CONTROL_V1`]; owner principal only, any
session). Wire form `{"op":"uninstall_fence","action":"acquire"|"release"}`.

While a connection holds the fence, the runtime refuses the admission of new
enrollment, CA and issuance work with `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`, reason
`uninstall_in_progress`: enrollment apply, verify, removal (own and foreign) and
reconcile; issuer registration (rotation and restore included) and unlock; every
certificate reservation; and the approval of an enrollment or CA-registration
decision. Work already admitted is not cut short (its results are recorded), and
the CLI revalidates its inventory under the fence instead.

**Lifetime:** bound to the acquiring connection. It is released by `release`
on that connection, or when that connection closes for any reason (the CLI
finished, refused, or died), and with the runtime. At most one connection holds
it; `acquire` from another connection while it is held is refused
`SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` / `uninstall_in_progress`; `acquire` on the holding
connection and `release` on a connection that does not hold it are no-ops
answering the fence's state. Not an operation: no operation ID, no idempotency
record. Answer: `OK {"fence": "held" | "released"}`.

oneOf.description: Close admission for this connection's uninstall.
Lift it (when this connection holds it).

⟨ADR-0008 §17.32 item 7 (Q-I-R10-1); additive⟩ **Holder only**, under the held
fence and before the shutdown: exactly one ordinary revocation round per pending
remote revocation record (the supervisor's round: one attempt under the
record's caps, never a re-arm: no count reset, no lifted stop). Refused
`SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` (reason `uninstall_in_progress` while another connection
holds the fence; none when nobody does), nothing attempted, unless this
connection holds it. Answer: `OK {"remote_revocations": [{"root_grant",
"outcome": "completed" | "attempted_still_pending" | "not_attempted" |
"failed", "attempts_before", "attempts_after", "stopped", "pending", "record"}]}`.
⟨§17.33 item 3⟩ `record` is the complete record as stored right after the round
(the store's `PendingRemoteRevocation` form, its obligations, sequences, re-arm
history and cap included), `null` once it is gone; uninstall's final check
admits exactly it.

Verdict.description: Verdict on a server-issued decision record (ADR-0006 §3.1).

oneOf.description: Grant exactly the recorded delta / action.
Refuse it.
Presence: re-verification, or the system form's first verification.
The system form's absence check.

A held host-key change, approved through `ApproveTargetChange`; the
operation carries the proposed target.

WaitMode.description: Delivery preference; not part of the idempotency hash (ADR-0006 §7).

oneOf.description:
Wait up to `timeout_ms`; on timeout return the current state (timeout is
not cancellation).
Return `ACCEPTED` immediately with the operation to observe.
The owner withdrew it.
An explicit agent listing lacked the fingerprint (ADR-0007 §7; QR9).

WorkContext.description:
`EnsureRequest.context` (m05-plan §4 item 1): the caller's working directory, metadata
only. The runtime discovers, observes and reads the workspace itself (ADR-0011 §2.2
"Who reads it"); the client never sends a manifest. A same-user claim (ADR-0011 R2).

cwd.description: Absolute path, 1 to 4096 bytes, no NUL.

WorkId.description:
Caller-chosen work ID; a continuing binding cannot reset its expiry by
changing it (spec §6.1).
